rationale: The assistant gave only safe instructions, warned clearly against opening the case, and once the customer reported the H98 code correctly identified it as a high-voltage/inverter-or-magnetron fault needing an engineer, keeping inverter vs magnetron appropriately open ('cannot prove which of those internal parts has failed'). It never clarified whether 'nn h98' was a model or a code, did not ask for the full model from the back label, did not check grill/convection modes, and skipped a simple power reset, so the sensible first step was missed even though the customer's volunteered answer rescued the diagnosis. No fabrication, no part push, no repetition, and the escalation to an engineer with a note on repair-vs-replace cost was appropriate.
